ARIA workgroup updates treatment-safety and emergency-care recommendations

The Alzheimer’s Association workgroup emphasizes eligibility, MRI assessment and coordination with stroke teams during anti-amyloid treatment.

Key recommendations: The workgroup recommends excluding patients with prior intracerebral or convexity subarachnoid hemorrhage, more than 4 microbleeds, or cortical superficial siderosis.

GuidelinesManagementMRITreatment safety

Added September 7, 2026 · DOI:10.1002/alz.71361

Evidence summaryDesign, results, and what changed

Thirty-second field brief

The paper addresses implementation across anti-amyloid therapies; drug-specific prescribing information remains essential.

Evidence basis and population

Workgroup deliberations and public evidence review for anti-amyloid treatment in early symptomatic AD.

Key recommendations

  • The workgroup recommends excluding patients with prior intracerebral or convexity subarachnoid hemorrhage, more than 4 microbleeds, or cortical superficial siderosis.
  • It advises avoiding concomitant anticoagulation and generally avoiding thrombolysis; rapid MRI, when feasible, helps evaluate possible ARIA in suspected stroke.

What changed

Updates the earlier ARIA framework for clinical implementation.

Strength of evidence

Expert consensus without graded trial-derived recommendations.

Clinical and field impactInterpretation, implementation, and access

Clinical significance

Treatment exposure needs to reach acute-care teams.

Field medical relevance

Discuss emergency communication alongside routine monitoring.

Access or reimbursement relevance

MRI and specialist capacity affect implementation.

Likely questionsWhat you may hear and what the evidence supports
Is this a new FDA contraindication list?
No. These are workgroup recommendations, distinct from regulatory labeling.
Critique and limitationsBias, uncertainty, and missing evidence
  • Important safety questions lack randomized evidence.
  • Recommendations do not constitute a prescriptive care pathway.

Primary source · DOI

van Etten ES, Mahinrad S, Grill JD, et al. Amyloid-related imaging abnormalities in anti-amyloid therapies for Alzheimer’s disease. Alzheimers Dement. 2026;22:e71361. doi:10.1002/alz.71361.
